      "Decadal climatology of groundwater recharge (QDRAI/QRECHARGE) beneath agricultural columns",

  },

feasibility.verdict: Partially feasible: single-column ELM can quantify natural recharge, ET, and vertical water-table dynamics, but it cannot represent anthropogenic groundwater pumping or lateral aquifer flow/recovery required to directly evaluate a 30% pumping-reduction scenario.
answerable: Decadal climatology of groundwater recharge (QDRAI/QRECHARGE) beneath agricultural columns
Simulated water-table depth (ZWT) response to climate forcing under natural (unpumped) vertical hydrology
Partitioning of ET vs runoff vs recharge that sets the water available to the aquifer
Soil moisture profile and drainage sensitivity across representative soil textures
Baseline recharge rates that can be fed as an upper boundary to an external aquifer/pumping model
not_answerable: Direct water-level recovery from a 30% pumping cut (ELM has no groundwater extraction term)
Lateral/regional aquifer flow and drawdown-cone recovery (requires a 3D groundwater model such as PFLOTRAN or MODFLOW)
Well-specific head recovery time series over the decade
Basin-scale water budget accounting for irrigation return flow and pumping

parsed.n_justification: Three columns span the dominant soil-texture and land-position gradient of the Upper Iowa basin (upland loess-derived silt loam, alluvial valley loam, and finer silty clay loam) so recharge and water-table sensitivity can be characterized across the agricultural landscape while remaining tractable for single-column runs.
requires_capabilities: ELM single-column (PTS_MODE) with active soil hydrology and variably-saturated column
GSWP3/CLMNCEP atmospheric forcing for 2005-2014 over the Upper Iowa domain
Coupling of ELM-derived recharge as a boundary condition to an external saturated-zone/pumping model (e.g., PFLOTRAN or MODFLOW) to actually simulate the 30% pumping-reduction recovery
assumptions: The 30% pumping-reduction impact on head recovery must be evaluated by a saturated-zone groundwater model driven by ELM recharge; ELM alone supplies the recharge flux, not the pumping response.
Crop/managed-vegetation PFT (rainfed corn-soy proxy) represents the agricultural land cover; irrigation withdrawal is not simulated in default ELM.
A 10-year forcing window (2005-2014) captures interannual recharge variability representative of a decadal recovery period.
Water-table dynamics use ELM's unconfined-aquifer (WA/ZWT) parameterization as a 1-D approximation, without lateral groundwater exchange.
